newsitem.title: INDIA: ICI expands India paints, sees Asia growth.
newsitem.headline: ICI expands India paints, sees Asia growth.

text.p: Britains' biggest chemical company, Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI) Plc expects continued sales growth for paint products in Asia although some markets are reaching maturity, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"Asia has got a number of markets that have slowed down, some of them are going from very high growth to mature growth, probably Thailand and Singapore...Taiwan," Peter Kirby, chief executive officer of ICI Paints, one of the main areas of the group's operations.
But ICI Paints remained bullish toward Asia as a few countries continued to show strong growth, he said.
"Quite a number of our Asian markets are continuing to grow strongly at the rate of about nine percent per year. We are not losing faith in Asia," Kirby told Reuters in an interview.
"We have already put about 12 new plants in Asia over the last few years and...have more than doubled our volumes in Asia."
Kirby was in India to open a paint factory belonging to ICI's 51 percent owned subsidiary, ICI India.
"We now see the opportunity to in fact double again and get a world market share of around 15 percent," Kirby said at the opening of the new factory at Thane, a town on Bombay's northern outskirts.
"The growth strategy of ICI India is based on a very major expansion of the paints business here," he said.
Presently, paints contributes about 40-42 percent of the Indian firm's total turnover. Officials said they planned to increase it to about around 50 percent in the next few years.
The other businesses of ICI India include explosives, chemicals and polyurethene.
ICI's Kirby said he was confident India will increase its five percent contribution to total Asian sales, but did not give any figures.
Since economic liberalisation began in 1991, India has experienced a combination of high industrial growth, rapid urbanisation and a much greater growth in its middle class, Kirby said.
"All of these helps to stimulate the paints market," he added.
Senior officals of ICI India forecast the company's turnover would grow about tenfold in sales by the year 2005.
In the six months ending September 1996, ICI India's sales totalled 3.06 billion rupees ($85 million), compared to 2.82 billion ($79 million) in the same period a year earlier.

The commissioning of the fully computerised Thane plant, costing 400 million rupees, will increase ICI India's production capacity to 50 million litres a year, with 40 million litres coming from the new factory.
ICI India also plans to commission a 20 million litre capacity paint plant, costing around 800 million rupees, early next year near Chandigarh, in the north Indian state of Punjab.
